parole.testo: From a Germanic language, compare Middle High German vride (“truce, protection, safety”), German Friede (“peace”).

From a Germanic language, possibly via Bavarian. Attested around 1405. Compare Middle High German lute, Early New High German laut, German Laute, from Old French leüt, from Arabic اَلْعُود (al-ʕūd, “wood, lute”, literally “the wood”).

parole.significato: mortar (a hollow vessel used to pound, crush, rub, grind or mix ingredients with a pestle)
parole.testo: From a Germanic language. Compare Middle High German morsær, German Mörser. The German word is from Latin mortārium (“mortar”). First attested in Hungarian in 1405.
From a Germanic language, compare German Schwager (“brother-in-law”).

parole.significato: palm (the inner part of the human hand)
parole.testo: Probably from a Germanic language. Compare Old High German tenar, Middle High German tëner (“palm”).
From a Germanic language, compare Middle High German snûr (“thread”), German Schnur (“string”).
